title: Lightning Behavior and Its Relationship with Topography, Precipitation, and Land Use in the São Francisco River Basin
datasets: ASTER Global Digital Elevation Model V003
TRMM Lightning Imaging Sensor (LIS) orbital lightning observations

idea.research_question: How do terrain and precipitation jointly explain spatial and seasonal variability in lightning activity across a river basin?
idea.hypothesis: Lightning flash-rate density responds nonlinearly to elevation and season, with precipitation modifying the strength and spatial distribution of the terrain relationship.
idea.mechanism: LIS/TRMM event observations are aggregated to a common grid; ASTER GDEM supplies elevation, slope and aspect; CHIRPS represents precipitation state. Seasonal threshold and interaction analyses test whether topographic control changes under distinct hydroclimatic regimes.

key_variables.target: Lightning flash-rate density, hotspot location and seasonal event-rate regime
predictors: ASTER GDEM elevation, slope and aspect

idea.analytical_approach: Common-grid aggregation, seasonal stratification, hotspot/cluster analysis, nonlinear threshold detection and terrain-by-precipitation/land-use interaction modelling.
idea.expected_contribution: A quantitative basin-scale framework for separating topographic, hydroclimatic and land-use controls on lightning risk.
idea.falsification_condition: Lightning rates show no reproducible association with terrain after precipitation and land-use adjustment, or the inferred thresholds are unstable across seasons and spatial cross-validation folds.
